body:
MYK'S RULING (2026-07-27, chat), and it supersedes the three options this ticket first
offered. The question was "may a connector retract what the operator wrote?" His answer changes the
frame: don't narrow the striker set, SCOPE THE AUTHOR.

The model, in his words: an MCP connection is scoped to a user. The user must already exist — the
operator provisions the account. Whoever holds that user's credential can then set up MCP as that
user. Everything that user writes is scoped to THAT USER'S CONTAINER. Inside it they are a full
author, negations included, and those negations BIND there. What they cannot do is reach the root
container without the operator accepting a promotion.

THIS IS ALREADY THE SPEC'S COMMITMENT. §28 says it outright — "Trust is a property of a CONTAINER",
"the operator's trust was never a special kind of trust; it is simply the root container's trust",
and "Admission delegates downward freely. Effectiveness attenuates." Its §28.1 already states the
negation half exactly: law admitted into a child binds within that child at most, and reaches the
parent only by promotion (§24.3's adoption-merge, where the operator re-signs it as their own claim
with a `loam.adoption` record). §28.2 calls a child container a quarantine relative to its parent.
So this is not a new design. It is §28 applied to IDENTITY rather than to federated law.

WHAT STANDS BETWEEN THE SPEC AND THE MODEL — three gaps, and the first two are the work:

(1) A CONTAINER HAS NO OPERATOR OF ITS OWN. `openContainerImpl` (src/gateway/container.ts) reads
`gw.operatorAuthor` and signs with `gw.options.seed` — the HOST's. The good news is that the
striker set is ALREADY parameterised the right way: `lawfulStrikersJson(operator, …)` in
src/gateway/accounts.ts computes trust relative to a given operator, so a container that carried its
own operator would get its own striker set almost for free. §28's "authority that is real at one
depth and inert at another" is the sentence to build to.

(2) THE DOORS HAVE NO PER-CONTAINER IDENTITY. The token table maps a token to `{ actor }` or
`{ operator: true }`, server-wide. There is no "actor of container C". The consequence is live today
and was found in T113's review: a container mount's write doors are open and share the host's
operator, so a user's token would open every mount rather than only theirs.

(3) §36's SESSION IS DELIBERATELY SERVER-WIDE, and T113 ships a guard that REFUSES to serve the
login doors beside a second mount, with the reason in the error: a session token cannot be scoped to
one mount yet. That guard is the honest admission of this gap. This ticket is what lifts it — which
is a good sign the guard was real rather than arbitrary.

TWO THINGS TO SETTLE INSIDE THE MODEL (the model recommends the first of each):
- Where does a user's container come from? Recommend: every NON-OPERATOR user gets one at creation,
  named for the user. The operator's own user writes to root, because it IS root's operator.
  The alternative is an explicit `--container` flag, which invites a user with no container.
- What does a promotion look like for a user's claim? Recommend §24.3's existing adoption-merge
  unchanged, so there is one promotion mechanism rather than a second one for users.

WHAT THIS BUYS BEYOND THE ORIGINAL QUESTION: multi-user becomes real; a credential's reach is
answered by "whatever its container permits" instead of by a scope vocabulary §37 deliberately does
not have; and the answer to "can this connector retract my claims" becomes NO by construction rather
than by a predicate somebody has to remember to apply.

RAILS, both sides: a user's negation binds for a reader INSIDE that user's container (or authorship
there has broken), AND the same negation does NOT bind for a reader at root (or the scoping did
nothing). Assert at both levels — the negation delta is in the ground either way; what changes is
what a reader through a Schema resolves at each depth. Plus: a promotion the operator accepts DOES
make it bind at root, or promotion is not the crossing §28 says it is.

DESIGN-STAGE: this changes what the trust root delegates, so the spec section is Myk's merge.
Neither T113 nor T114 is blocked — T113's guard is an honest refusal and T114's consent page now
states the powers a grant actually carries.
title: Scope a connector to a USER, and a user to a CONTAINER — §28's model applied to identity
